Bug_Details:
Classes that override equals should also override hashCode. The contract for Object.hashCode states that if two objects are equal, then
calling the hashCode() method on each of the two objects must produce the same
result. Implementing equals() but not hashCode() causes broken behaviour
when trying to store the object in a collection. See Effective Java 3rd Edition §11 for more information and a
discussion of how to correctly implement hashCode().
Bug_Explanation: The Person class overrides the equals() method but does not override the hashCode() method. This violates the contract where equal objects must have the same hash code, causing inconsistent behavior when instances are used in hash-based collections like HashSet.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testPersonHashSetBehavior' triggers the bug by attempting to verify if a HashSet containing 'person1' also considers an equivalent 'person2' object as a member. Due to the missing hashCode implementation in the Person class, even though 'person1' and 'person2' are equal according to the equals method, the HashSet fails to recognize 'person2' as an equivalent entry.
